## Circular to Licensed and Registered Persons Relaxation for Former Practitioners to Re-enter the Industry

To  facilitate  re-entry  into  the  industry,  the  SFC's  Academic  and  Accreditation  Advisory Committee has decided that former practitioners who had left the industry for between three to eight years may be exempted from the relevant competence examinations (including both industry  qualification  and  local  regulatory  framework)  when  they  re-apply  for  a  licence  or seek  to  be  re-engaged  by  a  registered  institution  as  a  relevant  individual  to  practise  in  the same regulated activity and role as before.  Hitherto only former practitioners who had been licensed  or  acting  as  a  relevant  individual  of  a  registered  institution  within  the  past  three years were exempted.

To be eligible for the new exemption, applicants must also meet at least one of the following requirements:

- Completion of five Continuous Professional Training (CPT) hours for each year of absence from the industry.  Regulatory training must make up at least 50% of the CPT activities;
- Attendance at a specialised course conducted by the Hong Kong Securities Institute in respect  of  securities  or  futures,  or  the  Vocational  Training  Council  in  respect  of leveraged foreign exchange. Course details will be announced  by the two organisations in due course.

This topic will be added to the 'Frequently Asked Questions' of the 'Competence' section in the SFC's website (www.hksfc.org.hk).

Licensing Department Intermediaries and Investment Products Division
